items.title: Section: Stage Four Opens — Cultivating the Path Already Attained

items.zh: 云何修習如所得道？謂彼如是所生廣大無罪歡喜，溉灌其心，為趣究竟，於現法中心極思慕。
items.en: How does one cultivate the path already attained? The vast, blameless joy thus generated irrigates the mind, and, in pursuit of the final goal, gives rise, in this very life, to the mind's most intense longing.

items.title: Stage Four Completes: Four Supports, Five Perfections

items.zh: 彼由如是心生思慕，出離樂欲數數現行。謂我何當能具足住如是聖處，如阿羅漢所具足住。如是欲樂生已，發勤精進，無間常委，於三十七菩提分法，方便勤修。又彼如是勤精進故，不與在家、出家眾相雜住，習近邊際諸坐臥具，心樂遠離。又彼如是發生欲樂、發勤精進，樂遠離已，不生喜足。謂於少分殊勝所證，心無喜足；於諸善法轉上、轉勝、轉微妙處，悕求而住。由此四法攝受修道，極善攝受。即此四種修道為依，如先所說諸歡喜事所生歡喜，彼於爾時修得圓滿。最極損減方便道理，煩惱斷故，獲得殊勝所證法故，亦令喜悅修得圓滿。又修所斷惑品麁重已遠離故，獲得輕安；輕安故生，身心清涼，極所攝受。如是二種修得圓滿。又此有學，金剛喻定到究竟故，修得圓滿。是名修習如所得道。又此修習如所得道義，廣說應知。謂四種法為依止故，能令五法修習圓滿。除此更無若過若增。
items.en: From this longing that has arisen in the mind, the wish for liberation repeatedly manifests: "When shall I be able to abide fully in such a noble state, as the arhats abide?" Once this wish has arisen, vigorous effort is aroused — unbroken and thoroughgoing — diligently applied through skilful means to the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment. Because of this vigorous effort, one no longer mingles with householders or renunciants indiscriminately, drawing near only the barest, simplest seat and bedding, the mind delighting in solitude. Having thus given rise to the wish for liberation, aroused vigorous effort, and come to delight in solitude, one no longer rests content with partial attainment, but abides seeking what is ever higher, ever more excellent, ever more subtle among wholesome states. By these four factors, the cultivation of the path is most excellently sustained. …Through the ultimate, most thoroughgoing means by which the afflictions are cut off, one attains the excellent realisation, and by this the perfection of delight is likewise accomplished. Further, because the coarse residue of the afflictions cut off through cultivation has already been removed, one attains ease of body and mind; because this ease has arisen, body and mind become cool and clear, most fully embraced by it. Thus these two are perfected through cultivation. Further, this trainee, having reached the diamond-like concentration in full, thereby perfects cultivation. This is called cultivating the path already attained. This meaning of cultivating the path already attained should be understood in full: relying on four factors, one brings five factors to perfection through cultivation. Beyond this, there is nothing further to exceed it, and nothing further to add.

items.zh: 云何證得極清淨道及果功德？
items.en: What is attaining the path of utmost purity together with the merit of its fruit?

items.title: Section: Stage Five Begins — The Fruit of Utmost Purity

items.zh: 謂於三位，樂位、苦位、不苦不樂位。為諸煩惱之所隨眠。有二種補特伽羅，多分所顯。一者、異生，二者、有學。又有二種能發起雜染品。一者、取雜染品，二者、行雜染品。即為斷此二雜染品，入善說法毘奈耶時，能為障礙所有煩惱。此諸煩惱，能為隨眠，深遠入心。又能發生種種諸苦。若能於此無餘永斷，名為證得極淨道果。
items.en: Regarding the three feeling-positions — pleasant, painful, and neither-pleasant-nor-painful — the afflictions lie dormant within them. Two kinds of persons chiefly display this: the ordinary being, and the trainee. There are, further, two forces capable of generating defilement: the defilement of grasping, and the defilement of karmic activity. It is precisely in order to cut off these two defilements that, upon entering the well-taught Dharma and discipline, the afflictions present themselves as obstacles. These afflictions, functioning as dormant tendencies, penetrate deeply into the mind, and further give rise to manifold sufferings. If one is able to cut these off entirely, without remainder, this is called attaining the fruit of utmost purity.

items.title: The Path of Utmost Purity: Ten Factors, Five Aggregates

items.zh: 又十無學支所攝五無學蘊，所謂戒蘊、定蘊、慧蘊、解脫蘊、解脫。知見蘊，名極清淨道。
items.en: Further, the five aggregates of the one beyond training, comprised by the ten factors beyond training — namely the aggregate of moral discipline, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation — this is called the path of utmost purity.

items.zh: 又由證得此極淨道，離十過失，住聖所住。云何名為十種過失？
items.en: Further, by attaining this path of utmost purity, one is free of ten faults and dwells in the dwelling of the noble ones. What are the ten faults?

items.title: Ten Faults an Arhat Never Has, and the Two Kinds of Nirvāṇa

items.zh: 所謂依外諸欲所有愁、歎、憂、苦種種惱亂，苦苦相應過失。又有依內不護諸根過失。由不護諸根故，生愁歎等。又有愛味樂住過失。又有行住放逸過失。又有外道不共，即彼各別邪見所起語言、尋思、追求三種過失。又有依靜慮邊際過失。又有緣起所攝，發起取雜染品過失。又有發起行雜染品過失。若於如是十種過失永不相應；唯有最後身所任持，第二餘身畢竟不起，於最寂靜涅槃界中，究竟安住。一切有情乃至上生第一有者，於彼一切所有有情得為最勝。是故說名住聖所住。以能遠離十種過失，又能安住聖所住處，故名功德。又若彼果、若極淨道、若彼功德，如是一切，總略說名證得極清淨道及果功德。又此證得極清淨道及果功德義，廣說應知如所說相。除此更無若過若增。
items.en: These are: the fault, associated with the suffering of suffering, of the various afflictions — grief, lamentation, distress, and pain — that depend on external sense-desires; the fault of leaving the senses unguarded within; the fault of savouring and clinging to the pleasure of meditative dwelling; the fault of laxity in both activity and stillness; the three faults, not shared with the noble teaching, of speech, deliberation, and pursuit that arise from various non-Buddhist wrong views; the fault of [mistaking] the outer limit of meditative absorption [for liberation]; the fault of generating the defilement of grasping, comprised within dependent origination; and the fault of generating the defilement of karmic activity. Whoever is permanently free of all ten of these faults — sustained only by this final body, with no second body ever to arise again — abides ultimately within the realm of utterly quiescent nirvāṇa. …This, therefore, is called abiding where the noble ones abide. Because one is able to stay far from these ten faults and to abide where the noble ones abide, this is called excellent quality. Whether it is this fruit, this path of utmost purity, or this excellent quality — all of this together is called, in brief, attaining the path and fruit of utmost purity... Beyond this, there is nothing further to exceed it, and nothing further to add.

items.zh: 若得如是最上無學諸聖法者，如是聖法相應之心，於妙五欲極為厭背；無異熟故，後更不續。若世間心雖復已斷，猶得現行。彼於後時任運而滅。又煩惱道後有業道，於現法中已永斷絕；由彼絕故，當來苦道更不復轉。由此因果永滅盡故，即名苦邊。更無所餘，無上、無勝。
items.en: When one has attained such supreme noble qualities of one beyond training, the mind associated with those noble qualities turns utterly away from the fine sense pleasures; because there is no ripening, there is no further continuation in the future. Although mundane states of mind have been cut off, they may still occur; but later they cease of their own accord. Further, the path of the afflictions and the path of action that follows it have already been permanently cut off in this present life; because they are cut off, the path of suffering no longer proceeds in the future. Because cause and effect have thus been permanently extinguished, this is called the end of suffering. There is nothing further beyond it; it is unsurpassed and unexcelled.

items.title: Fascicle Complete: The Entire Twelfth Ground Closes

items.zh: 此中若入聖諦現觀；若離障礙；若為證得速疾通慧作意思惟諸歡喜事；若修習如所得道；若證得極清淨道及果功德；如是名為出世間一切種清淨。又此出世間一切種清淨義，廣說應知如所說相。除此更無若過若增。如是若先所說世間一切種清淨，若此所說出世間一切種清淨，總略為一，說名修果。如是如先所說若修處所，若修因緣，若修瑜伽，若修果，一切總說為修所成地。
items.en: Here, whether it is entering the direct realisation of the noble truths; or removing the obstacles; or, in pursuit of swift, penetrating wisdom, applying the mind to the matters of joy; or cultivating the path already attained; or attaining the path and fruit of utmost purity — all of this together is called supramundane purity of every kind. This meaning of supramundane purity of every kind should, in full, be understood exactly as stated. Beyond this, there is nothing further to exceed it, and nothing further to add. Thus, whether it is the mundane purity of every kind spoken of earlier, or this supramundane purity of every kind spoken of here, taken together as one, this is called the fruit of cultivation. Thus, whether it is the basis for cultivation spoken of earlier, or the causes and conditions of cultivation, or the yogic practice of cultivation, or the fruit of cultivation — all of this together is called the Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation.

blocks.text: The last day of the Stage Attained Through Cultivation: from the path already attained to the arhat's utmost purity. Tomorrow begins the **Śrāvaka Stage**, the thirteenth stage and one of the longest in the treatise.

One gives rise to the wish for liberation, rouses vigorous effort, delights in solitude, and is never content: "by these four factors", the path already attained is cultivated further. At its culmination comes the **diamond-like concentration** (金剛喻定). Master Cháng Bǎi: it is strong like diamond and cuts through any subtle affliction.
Afflictions lie latent in the three kinds of feeling: pleasant, painful, neutral. With them uprooted, two liberations are attained (of mind and of wisdom).

The one beyond training has "five aggregates" of a new kind, made up of ten factors: right view through right knowledge and right liberation; grouped as moral discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.

subs.head: Ten faults an arhat never has

blocks.text: The arhat has none of the ten wrong factors. Master Cháng Bǎi: because right speech, right thought, right action, and right livelihood are fulfilled. When the body suffers, the arhat "receives only the first arrow", bodily pain, "and not the second", mental pain. Two nirvāṇas follow: with remainder, while the body lasts, and without remainder at its end.

Venerable Miào Jìng recaps: first the **place** of cultivation (favourable birth, inner and outer); then its **causes** (hearing, nirvāṇa as aim, ripening wisdom); then **the practice** (remedies, mundane and supramundane purity); then the **fruit**.

Hearing, reflection, cultivation: these three stages form the core of how this treatise thinks about learning. Hearing gives the material; reflection sorts and tests it; cultivation makes it one's own. The Śrāvaka Stage, which follows, will lay out the meditative path of the disciples in full detail.

quiz.q: Which four factors does the treatise say sustain the cultivation of the path?
options: the wish for liberation, vigorous effort, delight in solitude, and not resting content but seeking ever higher
quiz.why: Having given rise to the wish for liberation, aroused vigorous effort, come to delight in solitude, and not resting content — "by these four factors, the cultivation of the path is most excellently sustained." Master Cháng Bǎi: some stream-enterers stop practising, thinking that at most seven more lives will bring arhatship anyway.

quiz.q: "Having reached the diamond-like concentration in full, one perfects cultivation." How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it?
options: another name for the first absorption
concentration as strong as diamond, able to cut even the subtlest affliction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this concentration is strong like diamond and can cut through any subtle affliction.

quiz.q: In which three positions do afflictions lie dormant, and in which two kinds of persons are they chiefly displayed?
options: past, present, future; ordinary and non-Buddhist
body, speech, mind; lay and ordained
the three realms; gods and humans
pleasant, painful, neutral feeling-positions; ordinary beings and trainees
quiz.why: "Regarding the three feeling-positions — pleasant, painful, and neither-pleasant-nor-painful — the afflictions lie dormant within them. Two kinds of persons chiefly display this: the ordinary being, and the trainee." Master Cháng Bǎi: in pleasant states greed mostly arises, in painful states anger.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call "the path of utmost purity"?
options: the five aggregates of the one beyond training, comprised by the ten factors: discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation
quiz.why: "The five aggregates of the one beyond training, comprised by the ten factors beyond training — moral discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation — this is called the path of utmost purity." Venerable Miào Jìng: the arhat takes these five aggregates as his very life.

quiz.q: The note says the three non-Buddhist faults of speech, deliberation, and pursuit are removed by right speech, action, and livelihood. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: by four factors: right speech, right thought, right action, and right livelihood — the note omits right thought
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the arhat does not have them, because he has accomplished the virtues of right speech, right thought, right action, and right livelihood. The fault of deliberation is countered by right thought; the note lists only three factors.

quiz.q: For the first fault, "bound to the suffering of suffering," what image does Master Cháng Bǎi use to show the arhat is free of it?
options: two arrows — feeling bodily pain, the arhat takes only the first arrow, not the second, mental one
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when there is painful bodily feeling, the arhat receives only the first arrow — bodily pain — and not the second arrow of mental pain. The English "bound to sorrow" loses the technical term "suffering of suffering."

quiz.q: In the closing summary, "修處所" is rendered "the ground and ripening." What do the masters say it is?
options: the place of cultivation is favourable rebirth (inner and outer); the four domains and seven branches together form the Ground of Cultivation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: first is the place of cultivation — what is it? Favourable rebirth, divided into inner and outer. Master Cháng Bǎi: the place, causes, yogic practice, and fruit of cultivation — four domains and seven branches — together are the Ground of What Is Attained Through Cultivation. The English "ripening" has no basis.
